summary.core_scenario: A senior backend engineer, Tomás Vieira, responded defensively to corrective feedback delivered hurriedly and without follow-up. A subsequent sprint review exchange narrowed team participation, and a later outage touched the same area but does not prove causality. The manager must address observable behavioural impact without prosecuting technical decisions, without asserting causality, and without requiring agreement on root cause.

stakes.employee: Behavioural feedback may be interpreted as a challenge to technical competence.
stakes.manager: Must avoid prosecuting or retreating; must correct her own earlier process failure.
stakes.team: Reduced psychological safety and reduced participation in technical discussions.
stakes.organisation: Escalation path appears available but is not functioning.

ambiguity: Whether Tomás’s defensiveness is a stable pattern or a reasonable response to rushed feedback.
Whether his response caused the sprint-review silence.
Whether juniors are avoiding him specifically or due to rota/workstream changes.
Whether the outage is connected to the sprint review.
Whether Aoife’s preference for written questions reflects discomfort or working style.
Whether the manager’s earlier handling contributed materially.

evidence_pack.observed: Aoife raised a concern; Tomás responded; no action or owner assigned; participation narrowed.
evidence_pack.not_proven: That Tomás caused the silence; two attendees left early; later items were routine.

evidence_pack.observed: Junior routing to Tomás declined; his review volume and speed remain high.
evidence_pack.not_proven: Intent or cause; rota and workstream changes are confounders.

evidence_pack.observed: A senior observer noted juniors going quiet around Tomás.
evidence_pack.not_proven: Representativeness or impartiality; prior history exists; source cannot be named.

evidence_pack.observed: Outage involved invalidation path; multiple contributing factors; Tomás authored candid document.
evidence_pack.not_proven: Any link to sprint review; draft findings not final.

evidence_pack.observed: Accepted general concern; rebutted each specific example; at least one rebuttal appears correct.
evidence_pack.not_proven: That other examples were incorrect; scrutiny is reasonable when one example is mistaken.

evidence_pack.observed: Strong technical praise; two comments describe interactions as effortful.
evidence_pack.not_proven: Causality; sample is small, self-selected, anonymised, and predates events.

evidence_pack.observed: She asked about raising concerns in writing.
evidence_pack.not_proven: That this preference is caused by Tomás; she did not attribute it.

Impact stated as narrowed participation and lack of follow-up.
Separate direct observation from reported information.
No attribution of motive or causality.
prohibited: Using Nadia’s report as opening evidence.
ambiguity_to_preserve: Effect can be stated without asserting intent.

requirements: Explore what he thought Aoife was asking.
Explore what he noticed about participation.
Explore how he interpreted earlier feedback.
Surface manager’s own contribution (rushed, unclosed feedback).
prohibited: Correcting his account in real time.
Accepting procedural promises as exploration outcome.
ambiguity_to_preserve: Whether detail was driven by expertise, uncertainty, habit, or authority.

Treat hypotheses as working possibilities, not findings.
At least one manager-owned commitment addressing her earlier process failure.
At least one employee commitment addressing behaviour in defined context.
prohibited: Commitments requiring concession of technical position.
ambiguity_to_preserve: Commitments are experiments, not proof of cause.

requirements: Clarify what is not being said (role, rating, promotion, technical judgement).

acceptable: Defined pause, written-first approach, or taking one question offline.
Manager commitment addressing her own process failure.
unacceptable: Any commitment evaluable only by Tomás.
Any commitment requiring concession of technical correctness.

criteria: Bilateral commitments with dates and owners.
Silence stated as caused by Tomás.

focus: Clarify that discomfort is not failure.
Offer one alternative behaviour per failure.
Identify single stage where directness mattered.

sbi.title: Sprint Review: One Behaviour, One Effect
sbi.purpose: Name one observable behaviour from the sprint review and its immediate effect, without asserting motive or causality.
manager_guidance: Focus on the moment when Aoife raised a concern and Tomás responded.
State the immediate effect (participation narrowed, no owner assigned).
Avoid mentioning the outage or asserting causality.
sbi.input_prompt: Write a short SBI statement describing the sprint review moment you observed and its immediate effect, without claiming Tomás caused the silence.

exploration.title: Exploration: Tomás’s Account First
manager_guidance: What Tomás understood Aoife to be asking.
What he intended with his response.
What made examples hard to accept.
exploration.input_prompt: Write 3–5 exploration questions seeking Tomás’s account without accusing or asserting causality.

hypotheses.title: Hypotheses: Multiple Explanations, None Final
hypotheses.input_prompt: List 3–5 hypotheses you will keep open. Include your own contribution. None should be final findings.

commitments.title: Commitments: Observable Experiments, Shared Ownership
manager_guidance: One employee commitment in a defined meeting context.
One manager commitment addressing earlier process failure.
commitments.input_prompt: Define one employee commitment and one manager commitment. Each must be observable, owned, dated, and feasible before the checkpoint.

closing.title: Closing: Date, Owner, Open Status
manager_guidance: Clarify what is not being decided (role, rating, promotion, technical judgement).
closing.input_prompt: Write a closing statement naming the follow-up date, initiator, commitments, and open status.

behaviour_model_employee: Technically strong; responds to underspecified questions with detail and framing correction.
Accepts general behavioural concerns but scrutinises specific examples.
May interpret behavioural feedback as challenge to competence.
May remain composed, precise, and unconvinced while still making commitments.
May shift disagreement into written channels.
Must not be required to concede technical correctness or causality.
Must be allowed to disagree without disagreement ending the conversation.
behaviour_model_manager: Must name one observable behaviour and its effect.
Must elicit Tomás’s account before rebuttal.
Must acknowledge her earlier rushed, unclosed feedback.
Must avoid diagnosing personality or asserting causality.
Must close with dated checkpoint and explicit open status.
branching_constraints: Evidence challenge → avoid defensiveness; clarify evidence limits.
Composed disagreement → preserve ambiguity; maintain structure.
No branch may assert causality or motive.
No branch may convert outage into behavioural evidence.
commitment_constraints: Must be observable, owned, dated, feasible.
At least one manager-owned commitment addressing her earlier process failure.
At least one employee commitment addressing behaviour in defined context.
No commitments requiring Aoife’s undisclosed cooperation.
No commitments requiring concession of technical position.
closing_constraints: Must name follow-up date and initiator.
Must clarify what is not being said (role, rating, promotion, technical judgement).
Must establish continuity if context changes.
Must not introduce outage as leverage.
scoring_constraints: Excellent requires: specific behaviour named; impact stated; exploration elicited; multiple hypotheses; bilateral commitments; dated checkpoint.
Adequate requires: recognisable behavioural statement; some exploration; at least one concrete commitment; some next step.
Poor includes: outage used as evidence; causality asserted; attitudinal commitments; reassurance; no checkpoint.
feedback_constraints: Feedback must reference observable behaviours only.
Must not attribute motives, personality, or internal states.
Must identify specific moves and effects.
Must offer behavioural alternatives, not principles.
Must not treat agreement as required for success.
prohibitions: No causal claims not supported by evidence.
No promises about promotion, rating, progression, compensation, or future opportunity.
No use of outage as behavioural proof.
No use of Nadia’s report as decisive evidence.
No requirement for apology or emotional disclosure.
ambiguity_rules: Cause of routing shift remains unresolved.
Conversation ends with open question and date.
evidence_rules: Evidence must be used only within its limits.
Observed vs reported must be distinguished.
Anonymous report must not be treated as decisive.
Routing data must be treated as signal, not proof.
Peer feedback must be treated as limited and dated.
conversation_flow_rules: Stage 5: Close with dated checkpoint and open status.
